title: Asian Games 2026 Hockey Draw Places India and Pakistan on Collision Course for Knockouts
excerpt: Defending champions India drawn in Pool A with hosts Japan and South Korea, while Pakistan land in Pool B — setting up a potential semifinal or final clash in Kakamigahara.
body:
• India are in Pool A with Japan, South Korea, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia; Pakistan are in Pool B with Malaysia, China, Oman, Uzbekistan, and Thailand
  • The draw means an India-Pakistan clash can only happen in the semifinals or medal matches
  • The men's gold medallists earn an automatic berth at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics

The pool draw for the men's hockey competition at the 2026 Asian Games has been confirmed, and defending champions India find themselves in a demanding group that includes hosts Japan and South Korea. The hockey tournament will run from September 18 to October 3 at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Kakamigahara, Japan.

India have been placed in Pool A alongside Japan, South Korea, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia. Pakistan, India's arch-rivals in Asian hockey, are in Pool B with Malaysia, China, Oman, Uzbekistan, and Thailand, according to Olympics.com.

No Early India-Pakistan Showdown

The draw means one of Asian hockey's most anticipated fixtures — India versus Pakistan — cannot take place during the pool stage. If both teams finish in the top two of their respective groups, they could meet in the semifinals or, if they both advance further, in the gold medal match.

A total of 12 teams will compete in the men's tournament, divided into two pools of six. The top two teams from each group qualify for the semifinals, while the remaining teams play classification matches.

India's Squad and Recent Form

Hockey India announced the men's squad for the tournament on July 29, with veteran drag-flicker Harmanpreet Singh named captain. The 20-member squad includes experienced defenders Amit Rohidas and Jarmanpreet Singh, midfielders Hardik Singh, Manpreet Singh, and Vivek Sagar Prasad, and forwards Mandeep Singh and Abhishek.

India head to Aichi-Nagoya as the defending champions. They won gold at the Hangzhou 2023 Asian Games, defeating Japan 5-1 in the final. That victory, led by Harmanpreet Singh who scored a brace, secured India's fourth Asian Games gold medal and earned them direct qualification for the Paris Olympics.

Olympic Qualification on the Line

The 2026 edition carries stakes beyond continental bragging rights. The men's gold medallists will earn an automatic berth at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, making every pool match a step toward that prize. India joined South Korea as the second-most successful team in Asian Games men's hockey with four gold medals each; Pakistan lead with eight.

India's Path Through Pool A

India open their campaign against Indonesia on September 20, followed by Sri Lanka on September 22. The toughest pool-stage test comes on September 24 against South Korea, a traditional Asian hockey power. Japan, as hosts, will be motivated to perform before a home crowd at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.

India's men have been in strong form in recent international competitions, and the young talent coming through was evident when the U-18 men's team won the Asia Cup 2026 gold earlier this year in June, defeating Japan 4-1 in the final at the same Kakamigahara venue.

Women's Competition

In the women's tournament, India are in Pool B with Japan, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, and Uzbekistan. Pool A comprises China, South Korea, Malaysia, Kazakhstan, Chinese Taipei, and Bangladesh. The women's medal matches are scheduled for October 2, a day before the men's final.

With Olympic qualification at stake and a potential India-Pakistan knockout clash on the horizon, the hockey competition promises to be one of the marquee events at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
